Gallery Trail

  • Three different prints
1→2→3
  1. Each player solves the same sequence of three different prints.
  2. Match each print's last note to the next print's opening note.
  3. Keep chaining until all three prints are linked.

Encore Duet

  • Plain sticks
  1. Both players use plain sticks on the last frame to start the duet.
  2. Then take turns tapping the marked frames.

Coda Postcards

  • Plain glow ink
  • Plain paper
  1. After completing the duet, each player taps a score with plain glow ink.
  2. Tap normally to pick its closing note, or Sneak and tap to pick its opening note.
  3. After both players have picked, either one can stamp plain paper on the last frame.

Note blocks and chimes are covered in the full exploration guide on the hub.

Development preview

Postcard Pairs

  1. Hold a plain echo shard and tap framed signed postcards within 12 blocks.
  2. Your first tap anchors that postcard's chime and bell.
  3. Sneak while tapping to swap the chime and bell for that tap.
  4. Tap a second postcard whose opening chime matches the anchor's ending bell to link the pair.

Postcard Circuit optional

  1. After an echo-shard pair links, tap the third signed frame with plain prismarine crystals.
  2. All three frames must be within 12 blocks of each other.
  3. Sneak while tapping to swap that frame's chime and bell.
  4. The third frame's chime must match the second frame's bell, and its bell must match the first frame's chime.

Example: card 1, Sneak-tap card 2, then prismarine crystals on card 3 normally. The circuit closes and sounds Kite chime, Half Moon harp and Ember Peaks bell together.

Local development preview

Circuit Conductor optional

  1. After closing a circuit, tap any of its frames with a plain blaze rod. That frame is your starting corner.
  2. Keep tapping the frames in circuit order, then finish back on the starting frame: four taps in all.
  3. Sneak on the first tap to go backward around the circuit.

No timer, no bystander and no inventory cost. Example on the circuit above: Sneak-tap corner 2 first, then tap 2, 1, 3, 2.

    Development preview

    Circuit Counterpoint optional

    1. Finish a Conductor route on the circuit first. That completed route is the lead.
    2. Then tap the circuit's frames with a plain copper ingot to play the answer.
    3. Each answer tap is one corner ahead of the lead, in the same direction the route went: four taps in all.

    Example: the backward lead 2, 1, 3, 2 is answered with 1, 3, 2, 1.
